key_insight: AI and machine learning are transforming chemical engineering by combining data-driven methods with first-principles models to improve prediction, design, and decision-making across scales from atoms to industrial processes.
engineering_relevance: The main engineering value is more robust, interpretable, and scalable solutions for materials discovery, transport, separations, process systems, and operations under real-world constraints.
method: Integration with conservation laws and thermodynamic consistency
Human-AI collaboration at the right abstraction level
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes representative applications and methodological trends across atomic-scale simulation, materials discovery, transport, separations, process systems engineering, and industrial operations rather than reporting a single benchmark study.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is that black-box models may struggle with data scarcity, extrapolation, interpretability, and lifecycle management without strong domain constraints.
paper_title: Atoms to Processes: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Chemical Engineering
